requirements.title: Toolset and the new Config shape
requirements.rationale: Splitting the tool side out of Config is what lets an embedder build and use it without a model.

criteria.action: export a struct `Toolset` with exactly five fields in this order: `Tools []core.Tool`, `Policy core.ToolPolicy`, `Guard core.BeforeToolCall`, `After core.AfterToolCall`, `Events func(core.Event)`
criteria.contract: fields are Tools []core.Tool, Policy core.ToolPolicy, Guard core.BeforeToolCall, After core.AfterToolCall, Events func(core.Event), in that order; there are no other fields

setup: the root package agentkit
check.pseudocode: t = TypeOf(Toolset{}); assert names(t) == [Tools,Policy,Guard,After,Events]; assert type(Events) == func(core.Event)

criteria.action: define `Config` with exactly twelve fields in this order: `Client`, `Provider`, `Model`, `Effort`, `System`, `Prefix`, `Toolset`, `MaxTurns`, `MaxCostUSD`, `Timeout`, `Prune`, `MaxTokens`, with no `Tools`, `Policy`, `Guard` or `After` field, alias or forwarder
criteria.contract: field names in order are Client, Provider, Model, Effort, System, Prefix, Toolset, MaxTurns, MaxCostUSD, Timeout, Prune, MaxTokens; Tools, Policy, Guard and After are absent; the Toolset field has type agentkit.Toolset

setup: the root package agentkit
check.pseudocode: assert names(TypeOf(Config{})) == [12 names]; assert no field named Tools|Policy|Guard|After

criteria.condition: `New` is called with a valid client and model and a zero-value `Toolset`
criteria.action: return an agent with no tools
criteria.contract: non-nil `*Agent` and nil error; `a.Runner().Tools()` has length 0 and the first model request carries no tool definitions

setup: a scripted provider that records requests and answers with a final text message
a valid model
check.pseudocode: a,err = New(Config{Provider:p, Model:m}); assert err==nil; assert len(a.Runner().Tools())==0; a.Run(ctx,"hi"); assert len(p.requests[0].Tools)==0

requirements.title: NewRunner validates a toolset
requirements.rationale: Error parity with today's `New` is the acceptance criterion for moving validation.

criteria.condition: `NewRunner(ts)` is called
criteria.action: run `checkTool` on every entry of `ts.Tools`, then compute `ts.Policy.Resolve(ts.Tools)`, then run `checkTool` on every resolved tool, then run `checkShellGuard(ts.Guard, resolved)`, and return the first error any step produces
criteria.contract: `(*Runner, nil)` when every step passes; `(nil, err)` with the first failing step's error otherwise

setup: a toolset whose first tool has neither Handler nor Execute and which also exposes an unguarded shell tool
a toolset whose policy-resolved set contains a tool with both Handler and Execute
a valid toolset with a guard
check.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(ts1); assert r==nil && contains(err,'has neither Handler nor Execute'); ...

criteria.condition: a tool in `ts.Tools` or in the resolved set sets neither or both of `Handler` and `Execute`
criteria.action: refuse the toolset
criteria.contract: nil `*Runner` and an error whose text is `agentkit: tool %q has neither Handler nor Execute` or `agentkit: tool %q sets both Handler and Execute; exactly one`

setup: tool "t" with no Handler and no Execute
tool "u" with both Handler and Execute
check.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:[t]}); assert r==nil; assert err.Error()==want

criteria.condition: the tools' `ReachableTools` form a cycle by name, or a wrapper reaches a `Terminating` tool
criteria.action: refuse the toolset
criteria.contract: nil `*Runner` and an error whose text is `agentkit: reachable tools cycle detected: a -> b -> a` (the cycle path) or `agentkit: terminating tool %q cannot be reached through wrapper %q`

setup: tools a -> b -> a by ReachableTools names
a wrapper "codemode" reaching a tool marked Terminating
check.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(cyclicPair()); assert r==nil; assert err.Error()=='agentkit: reachable tools cycle detected: a -> b -> a'

criteria.condition: a shell tool is reachable in the resolved set, directly or through a wrapper, and `ts.Guard` is nil
criteria.action: refuse the toolset
criteria.contract: nil `*Runner` and an error for which `errors.Is(err, core.ErrUnguardedExecute)` is true, whose text contains `Toolset.Guard is nil`, does not contain `Config.Guard`, and ends with ` (tool %q)` or ` (wrapper %q reached shell tool %q)`

setup: a direct shell tool "run_command" and a wrapper reaching a shell tool, each with nil Guard
check.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:[shell]}); assert errors.Is(err, ErrUnguardedExecute); assert HasSuffix(err.Error(), ' (tool "run_command")')

criteria.action: for any toolset `ts`, return a non-nil error exactly when `agentkit.New(Config{Provider: p, Model: m, Toolset: ts})` with a valid provider and model returns one, with identical error text
criteria.contract: `NewRunner(ts)` error text == `New(cfg)` error text for every toolset in the test corpus, including valid ones (both nil)

setup: a stub provider and model so New passes its client and model checks
check.pseudocode: for ts in gen(): _,e1 = NewRunner(ts); _,e2 = New(Config{...,Toolset:ts}); assert (e1==nil)==(e2==nil); if e1 != nil: assert e1.Error()==e2.Error()

criteria.condition: the caller modifies or appends to the `ts.Tools` slice it passed after `NewRunner` returned
criteria.action: keep its tool set unchanged
criteria.contract: `r.Tools()` returns the same tool names before and after the caller's mutation

setup: a Tools slice with tools alpha and beta
check.pseudocode: r = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:s}); s[0]=other; s=append(s,gamma); assert names(r.Tools())==[alpha,beta]

criteria.action: allow `Call`, `Batch`, `Tools` and `Reachable` to be invoked from any number of goroutines at once without data races, keeping no mutable state after construction
criteria.contract: a test running 16 goroutines of concurrent `Call` and `Batch` passes under `go test -race`

setup: a runner over echo tools and a code-mode-like wrapper, with Guard, After and Events set to concurrency-safe functions
check.pseudocode: wg; for i in 0..16: go func(){ r.Call(...); r.Batch(...); r.Tools(); r.Reachable() }

requirements.title: What a runner and an agent expose
requirements.rationale: Models, MCP servers and prompts all need the resolved set the runner will actually run.

criteria.action: return the policy-resolved tool set in policy order as a fresh slice on every call
criteria.contract: result equals `ts.Policy.Resolve(ts.Tools)` by name and order; overwriting an element of a returned slice does not change the next call's result

setup: a ToolPolicy that reorders or filters the tools
check.pseudocode: a = r.Tools(); a[0]=core.Tool{}; b = r.Tools(); assert names(b)==names(policy.Resolve(tools))

criteria.action: return `core.ReachableTools` computed over the resolved set
criteria.contract: result equals `core.ReachableTools(r.Tools())` by name and order

setup: a toolset containing a wrapper declaring ReachableTools
an agent built from the same toolset
check.pseudocode: assert names(r.Reachable())==names(core.ReachableTools(r.Tools())); assert names(a.ReachableTools())==names(a.Runner().Reachable())

criteria.action: return from `ReachableTools()` the same tools as `a.Runner().Reachable()`
criteria.contract: names and order are equal

criteria.action: export exactly six methods on `*Agent`: `Run`, `Stream`, `Messages`, `Usage`, `ReachableTools` and `Runner`
criteria.contract: reflection over `*Agent`'s method set yields exactly these six names

setup: the root package
check.pseudocode: assert sorted(methodNames(TypeOf(&Agent{}))) == [6 names]

requirements.title: Runner.Call runs one call
requirements.rationale: A single entry point that always yields a result lets any caller run a tool exactly as the model would.

criteria.condition: `Call(ctx, name, input)` is invoked
criteria.action: run the call as a batch of one through the `Batch` implementation, with an id generated by `newID("call")`, and return that call's result without returning a Go error or panicking
criteria.contract: one `core.ToolResult`; the `ToolUseID` seen by `Guard` and the events matches `^call_[0-9a-f]{16}$`

setup: a runner with an echo tool, a Guard and an Events sink recording ids
check.pseudocode: res = r.Call(ctx,'echo',raw); assert res.OK; assert regexp('^call_[0-9a-f]{16}$').match(guardSeenID)

criteria.condition: `input` is empty or contains only whitespace
criteria.action: treat the input as `{}`
criteria.contract: `Guard` receives `RawInput` `{}` and a tool with no required arguments runs with `OK` true

setup: a tool with no required arguments and a Guard recording RawInput
check.pseudocode: for in in [nil,'','  \n']: res=r.Call(ctx,'noargs',in); assert res.OK; assert guard.raw=='{}'

criteria.condition: `name` is not in `Tools()`
criteria.action: return an error result without running any handler or guard
criteria.contract: `OK` false, code `unknown_tool`, text `no tool named %q is available in this run; available tools: …` identical to the text a run produces

setup: a runner with tools alpha and beta, a counting Guard
check.pseudocode: res=r.Call(ctx,'missing',{}); assert !res.OK && code=='unknown_tool'; assert res.LLMText()==unknownToolMessage('missing', byName)

criteria.condition: `input` is not a JSON object, the arguments fail schema validation, or the guard returns `Arguments` that JSON cannot encode
criteria.action: return an error result without running the handler
criteria.contract: `OK` false, code `invalid_arguments`; the handler's invocation count is 0

setup: a tool with a required string argument and a counting handler
a Guard that returns Arguments containing a channel value for another call
check.pseudocode: for in in ['not json','{}']: assert code(r.Call(ctx,'t',in))=='invalid_arguments'; assert handlerCalls==0

criteria.condition: `Guard` returns a decision with `Block` true
criteria.action: return an error result without running the handler, carrying the guard's reason or `blocked by policy` when the reason is empty
criteria.contract: `OK` false, code `blocked_by_policy`, text containing the reason; `Terminate` equals the decision's `Terminate`

setup: a Guard blocking with reason "no way" and Terminate true, a Guard blocking with empty reason, and a counting handler
check.pseudocode: res=r.Call(...); assert code=='blocked_by_policy'; assert res.Terminate==dec.Terminate

criteria.condition: the tool's handler panics or its `Handler` returns an error
criteria.action: recover the panic or capture the error and return it as a result
criteria.contract: `OK` false with code `panic` for a panic or `handler_error` for a `Handler` error; `Call` returns normally

setup: a tool whose handler panics
a tool whose Handler returns an error
check.pseudocode: assert code(r.Call(ctx,'boom',{}))=='panic'; assert code(r.Call(ctx,'fail',{}))=='handler_error'

criteria.condition: the context is done before the handler would start
criteria.action: return an aborted result without starting the handler
criteria.contract: `OK` false, code `aborted`, text `Operation aborted`; the handler's invocation count is 0

setup: an already cancelled context and a counting handler
check.pseudocode: cancel(); res=r.Call(ctx,'echo',{}); assert code=='aborted' && text=='Operation aborted'; assert calls==0

criteria.condition: `Guard` is invoked for a call made through `Call`
criteria.action: pass a `BeforeToolCallContext` with `ToolName`, `ToolUseID`, `Tool`, `Arguments` and `RawInput` filled as in a run, `Batch` holding the one call, `Index` 0, `Assistant` nil, `TurnCount` 0 and empty `ParentToolUseID` and `ParentToolName`
criteria.contract: ToolName is echo, ToolUseID matches call_<16 hex>, Tool is the echo tool, Arguments and RawInput are filled; Batch has exactly one call with that id, Index is 0; Assistant is nil, TurnCount is 0; ParentToolUseID and ParentToolName are empty

setup: a Guard recording its BeforeToolCallContext
check.pseudocode: g=rec; r.Call(...); assert g.Assistant==nil && g.TurnCount==0 && g.Index==0 && len(g.Batch)==1

requirements.title: Runner.Batch runs a batch with the driver's rules
requirements.rationale: Programmatic callers and the loop must get the same ordering, abort and concurrency semantics.

criteria.condition: `Batch(ctx, calls...)` is invoked with one or more calls
criteria.action: in a sequential prepare phase, emit a `ToolExecutionStartEvent` for each call in call order and run argument preparation and `Guard` in call order before any handler starts, finalizing unknown-tool, invalid-argument and blocked calls inline with the codes of 21-REQ-4
criteria.contract: start events arrive in call order; every `Guard` invocation precedes every handler start

setup: a runner with three calls (known, unknown, invalid-arguments, blocked mix) and an Events sink, a Guard and handlers recording a shared timeline
check.pseudocode: timeline index of last guard < index of first handler; starts order == calls order

criteria.condition: the context is done when the prepare phase ends
criteria.action: close every call not yet finalized as aborted, including calls the prepare loop never reached, and run no handler
criteria.contract: each such call's result has code `aborted` and text `Operation aborted`; handler invocation count is 0; each such call gets a start and an end event

setup: three calls; a Guard that cancels the context while preparing call 1, counting handlers
check.pseudocode: assert handlerCalls==0; for i in unfinalized: assert code(res[i])=='aborted'; assert starts[i] && ends[i]

criteria.action: run handlers concurrently with one goroutine per call joined by a `sync.WaitGroup` when there are at least two runnable calls and none targets a `Sequential` tool, run them one at a time in call order otherwise, and finalize each call (`After`, end event, result event) under a mutex scoped to the batch
criteria.contract: two blocking handlers in one batch overlap in time; with a `Sequential` tool present they never overlap; no two `After` invocations of one batch overlap

setup: two handlers that each block until both have started, a second batch including a Sequential tool, an After that records entry and exit
check.pseudocode: barrier handlers: both reach barrier within timeout; sequential: max concurrent == 1; After: max concurrent == 1

criteria.action: return exactly one result per call in call order whatever order the handlers finish in, and return an empty slice emitting no event when called with zero calls
criteria.contract: `len(results) == len(calls)` and `results[i]` belongs to `calls[i]`

setup: handlers that finish in reverse order of the calls
a call with empty ID
a Guard recording its context and an Events sink
check.pseudocode: res=r.Batch(ctx,c0,c1,c2); assert res[i].text==expected[i]; assert len(r.Batch(ctx))==0 && events==[]

criteria.action: use each call's `ID` verbatim, including an empty one, and pass `Guard` a context with `Batch` equal to `calls`, `Index` equal to the call's position, `Assistant` nil and `TurnCount` 0
criteria.contract: `BeforeToolCallContext.ToolUseID` and the events' `ToolUseID` equal `calls[i].ID`

criteria.action: set each result's `Terminate` to the call's final vote: the handler's `Terminate` unless `After` returned a non-nil `Terminate` which replaces it, `true` for a wrapper whose nested call was terminated by an interceptor, and the guard decision's `Terminate` for a blocked call
criteria.contract: the handler vote stands without After; a non-nil After decision replaces the handler vote; the terminated wrapper has Terminate true; the blocked call's Terminate equals the guard decision's

setup: a handler voting Terminate
an After returning Terminate=false for it
an After returning Terminate=true for a non-voting handler
a wrapper whose nested call was terminated by an interceptor
a call blocked by a guard with Terminate true
check.pseudocode: assert res[0].Terminate==true; assert res[1].Terminate==false; assert res[2].Terminate; assert res[3].Terminate; assert res[4].Terminate

criteria.action: for any batch of calls run with a nil `After`, return results whose `LLMText()` equals the text block of the `ToolResultMessage` the same calls produce in an agent run
criteria.contract: property test over generated batches mixing ok, error, unknown, invalid and blocked calls

setup: a scripted provider that emits the generated calls in one assistant message
an identical toolset used for a runner
check.pseudocode: for calls in gen(): res=runner.Batch(ctx,calls...); a.Run(...); msgs=toolResultMsgs(a.Messages()); for i: assert res[i].LLMText()==msgs[i].Content[0].Text

criteria.condition: an `After` interceptor edits `AfterToolCallContext.Result` in place
criteria.action: carry the edited message in the call's `ToolResultEvent` and in a run's transcript while leaving the returned `core.ToolResult` unedited
criteria.contract: `ToolResultEvent.Message` shows the edit; the returned result's `LLMText()` is the handler's text

setup: an After that rewrites AfterToolCallContext.Result's text to "edited"
an Events sink recording events; an agent run over the same toolset
check.pseudocode: res=r.Call(...); assert ev.Message.text=='edited'; assert res.LLMText()=='orig'

requirements.title: Nested calls run through the runner
requirements.rationale: A wrapper such as code mode must work from `Runner.Call` without an agent.

criteria.condition: a tool that declares `ReachableTools` is invoked through `Call`, `Batch` or an agent run
criteria.action: attach a `core.NestedCaller` to the handler's context that gives each nested call a fresh id from `newID("nested")` and runs it through preparation, `Guard`, the handler and `After`
criteria.contract: nested ids match `^nested_[0-9a-f]{16}$`

setup: a wrapper tool that calls core.CallNested on an echo tool, a Guard and After recording contexts, an Events sink
check.pseudocode: assert regexp(nestedID); assert guardCtx.ParentToolUseID==wrapperID; assert count(ToolResultEvent)==1

criteria.condition: a wrapper calls a tool that is not among its declared, policy-resolved reachable tools
criteria.action: return an error result for that call without running it
criteria.contract: code `unknown_tool` with text beginning `%s cannot call %q: ` followed by the unknown-tool message

setup: a wrapper reaching only echo, and another tool other in the runner
check.pseudocode: res,_=CallNested(ctx,{name:'other'}); assert code=='unknown_tool'; assert HasPrefix(text,'wrapper cannot call "other": ')

criteria.condition: a nested call runs
criteria.action: pass `ParentToolUseID` and `ParentToolName` to `Guard` and `After`, emit start and end events carrying `ParentToolUseID`, emit no `ToolResultEvent`, and return a guard block as a `blocked_by_policy` result

criteria.condition: `Guard` returns `Block` with `Terminate`, or `After` votes `Terminate`, for a nested call
criteria.action: make that and every later `CallNested` from the wrapper return `core.ErrTerminated` and set the wrapper's final vote to true
criteria.contract: `errors.Is(err, core.ErrTerminated)` is true; the wrapper's result has `Terminate` true

setup: case A: Guard blocks the nested call with Terminate
case B: After votes Terminate for the nested call
the wrapper makes a second nested call afterwards
check.pseudocode: _,err=CallNested(...); assert errors.Is(err,ErrTerminated); assert res.Terminate

criteria.condition: a nested handler returns a result with `Terminate` true
criteria.action: drop the vote and annotate both results
criteria.contract: the nested result's text contains `terminate vote ignored: `, the wrapper's contains `nested terminate vote ignored`, and the wrapper's `Terminate` is false

setup: a nested tool whose handler returns Terminate true
check.pseudocode: assert contains(nested.text,'terminate vote ignored: '); assert contains(res.text,'nested terminate vote ignored'); assert !res.Terminate

criteria.condition: the context is cancelled before a nested handler completes
criteria.action: return the nested call as aborted
criteria.contract: code `aborted`, text `Operation aborted`

setup: a wrapper that cancels the context before calling a nested tool, a counting nested handler
check.pseudocode: cancel(); res,_=CallNested(ctx,call); assert code=='aborted' && text=='Operation aborted'

criteria.condition: a `code_mode` tool built over `tools.For(ws, …)` is called through `Runner.Call` with a script that calls `read_file` on a workspace file
criteria.action: run the script and the nested `read_file` call with no agent and no provider
criteria.contract: `OK` true with the file content in the result text; `Toolset.Events` receives a `ToolExecutionStartEvent` and a `ToolExecutionEndEvent` for `read_file` whose `ParentToolUseID` is the `code_mode` call's id

setup: a temp workspace with a.txt, opened with workspace.Open and tools.For
a code_mode tool built over the tools, an Events sink recording events, no agent and no provider
check.pseudocode: ws=workspace.Open(dir); ts=tools.For(ws,Options{}); cm=codemode.New(ts...); r=NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:append(ts,cm),Events:rec}); res=r.Call(ctx,'code_mode',script)

criteria.condition: a tool that declares no `ReachableTools` calls `core.CallNested`
criteria.action: attach no nested caller to that tool's context
criteria.contract: `CallNested` returns `core.ErrNoNestedCaller`

setup: a tool with no ReachableTools whose handler calls core.CallNested
check.pseudocode: _,err=CallNested(ctx,call); assert errors.Is(err,core.ErrNoNestedCaller)

requirements.title: Execution events
requirements.rationale: Outside a run, events are the only way to observe recovered panics and the message `After` produced.

criteria.condition: a runner runs calls outside an agent run
criteria.action: deliver to `Toolset.Events` a `ToolExecutionStartEvent` and a `ToolExecutionEndEvent` for every call (with `ParentToolUseID` set on nested ones), a `ToolResultEvent` for each top-level call carrying the message as `After` left it, and a `core.ErrorEvent` for each panic recovered in `PrepareArguments`, `Guard`, a handler or `After`
criteria.contract: each call has a start and an end event; each top-level call has a ToolResultEvent carrying the message as After left it; each recovered panic produces one core.ErrorEvent

setup: tools that panic in PrepareArguments-time hooks, in Guard, in a handler and in After, an Events sink recording events
check.pseudocode: assert count(ErrorEvent)==4; for c: assert has(start,c) && has(end,c) && has(result,c)

criteria.condition: `Toolset.Events` is nil
criteria.action: discard the events and run the calls unchanged
criteria.contract: `Call` and `Batch` return the same results as with a sink and do not panic

setup: two runners over the same tools, one with Events nil and one with a recording sink
check.pseudocode: assert equal(r1.Call(...), r2.Call(...))

criteria.action: for any call, deliver its start event before its end event, and for a top-level call its end event before its `ToolResultEvent`
criteria.contract: property over concurrent batches and nested calls

setup: an Events sink recording a per-id sequence under a mutex
check.pseudocode: for batch in gen(): events=run(batch); for id: idx(start)<idx(end); if top: idx(end)<idx(result)

criteria.condition: `Toolset.Events` panics while handling an event
criteria.action: recover the panic, drop that event, and not report it again
criteria.contract: `Call` returns the call's normal result; no `ErrorEvent` for the sink's panic is delivered

setup: an Events sink that panics on every event and counts invocations
check.pseudocode: res=r.Call(...); assert res.OK; assert errorEventsForSinkPanic==0

criteria.action: invoke `Toolset.Events` from the goroutines running the calls without holding any runner-wide lock, so a sink that itself calls `Runner.Call` completes
criteria.contract: a sink calling `r.Call` from inside `Events` returns within the test timeout; `(*core.EventStream).Push` works as a sink under `-race`

setup: an Events sink that calls r.Call on a second tool when it sees the first start event
a second runner whose Events is (*core.EventStream).Push
check.pseudocode: done=make(chan); go func(){r.Call(...);close(done)}(); select{done; timeout fail}

criteria.condition: an agent run is executing tool calls
criteria.action: emit those calls' events to the run's `core.EventStream` and not call `Toolset.Events` for them
criteria.contract: `Toolset.Events` invocation count for the run's calls is 0; the run's stream receives the full sequence

setup: an agent with Toolset.Events counting invocations and a scripted provider returning one tool call then a final answer
check.pseudocode: collect stream; assert has(start,end,result); assert eventsCount==0

requirements.title: The agent is built on a runner
requirements.rationale: The pipeline must exist once, with the loop as one consumer.

criteria.condition: `New(cfg)` is called
criteria.action: check `Client`/`Provider` and then `Model` first, then call `NewRunner(cfg.Toolset)` and return its error unchanged without sending any request
criteria.contract: on a toolset failure: nil `*Agent`, error text identical to `NewRunner`'s, and the provider's request count is 0

setup: a recording provider, a toolset with an unguarded shell tool
a Config with no model and a bad toolset
check.pseudocode: _,e1=NewRunner(ts); a,e2=New(cfg); assert a==nil && e1.Error()==e2.Error() && p.requests==0

criteria.action: build request tool definitions (`core.ToolWires`), the system prompt (`prompt.Build`) and the fixed-token estimate from `Runner.Tools()`
criteria.contract: the request's tool names equal `a.Runner().Tools()` names in order

setup: a Policy that filters or reorders tools, a recording scripted provider
check.pseudocode: assert names(p.requests[0].Tools)==names(a.Runner().Tools())

criteria.action: return the agent's runner, the same pointer on every call, and remain callable while a run is in flight
criteria.contract: pointer equality across calls; calling it during `Run` does not return or cause `core.ErrBusy`

setup: an agent whose scripted provider blocks mid-run, an Events sink recording events
check.pseudocode: assert a.Runner()==a.Runner(); before=len(a.Messages()); a.Runner().Call(...); assert len(a.Messages())==before && a.Usage()==u

criteria.condition: a call is made through `a.Runner().Call` or `Batch`, during or outside a run
criteria.action: keep the call outside every run: add nothing to the transcript, add nothing to `Agent.Usage`, leave the run slot unclaimed, and send its events to `Toolset.Events`
criteria.contract: `a.Messages()` length and `a.Usage()` unchanged; a concurrent `Run` is not refused with `ErrBusy`

criteria.condition: a model response contains tool calls and its stop reason is not `max_tokens`
criteria.action: hand the calls to the runner's batch implementation with the run's stream as sink, the assistant message and turn count for the guard context, and a context carrying `core.WithUsageReporter(ctx, a.addUsage)`, record the returned `ToolResultMessage`s as `After` left them, and end the run with the terminate stop reason when any call's final vote is true
criteria.contract: `Guard` sees a non-nil `Assistant` and the turn number; the transcript holds one tool result message per call

setup: a Guard recording its context, a scripted provider returning two tool calls (one voting Terminate) in one assistant message
check.pseudocode: assert g.Assistant!=nil && g.TurnCount==1; assert len(toolResultMsgs)==2; assert stop==StopReasonTerminate

criteria.action: produce the same transcript, event sequence and order, stop reasons, model-visible texts and error texts as before this change, keeping `synthesizeTruncated` in `loop.go` for `max_tokens` responses
criteria.contract: the root module's loop, batch, nested-call, golden and scripted tests pass with only their `Config` literals migrated

setup: the root module's loop, batch, nested, golden and scripted tests migrated only in their Config literals
a max_tokens response with tool calls
check.pseudocode: go test . (existing golden_test, loop_test, batch_test, nested_test); assert handlerCalls==0 for length stop

criteria.action: define the batch executor and nested caller once, on the runner: `*Agent` has no `executeBatch` method, and only the runner's implementation calls `core.PrepareArguments`, `callBefore`, `invokeHandler` and `callAfter` in the root package
criteria.contract: an AST check of the root package's non-test files finds those call sites only in functions whose receiver or call chain belongs to the runner

setup: the root package non-test Go files parsed with go/parser
check.pseudocode: parse files; assert !hasMethod('Agent','executeBatch'); for call in callsTo(names): assert recvOf(enclosing(call)) in runnerTypes

criteria.condition: a runner runs calls outside an agent run
criteria.action: attach no usage reporter of its own and pass through any reporter the caller's context already carries
criteria.contract: a handler's `core.ReportUsage` reaches the caller's reporter when one is attached and is a no-op otherwise; `Agent.Usage` is unchanged

setup: a handler calling core.ReportUsage
a context carrying a counting reporter, and a plain context
